title: Durably store the proposed GraphRevisionContent body and seal a recomputed full content hash on the production propose/finalize path
description:
Filed by architect-0975cd3a 2026-08-22 ~11:2xZ as the measured prerequisite for task-eacea969's APPROVE leg (DoD[0]). The governor's split ruling said the approve leg has "ZERO unmet dependencies at HEAD" and invited disagreement "with a measurement, not a plan" — this is that measurement (3-lens panel wf_95dcf681 at HEAD 02ae4d2). The approve leg's writer exists to be built, but its INPUTS are absent, so DoD[0] cannot commit an honest ACTIVE revision and its accepted control could only seed the body through a fixture — the mock-backed accepted path rail 2 forbids.

THE GAP, symbol by symbol:
1. NO DURABLE PROPOSAL BODY. `readGraphBody(store, projectId, graphContentHash)` (apps/daemon/src/planning/graph-body-record.ts:163) answers GRAPH_BODY_ABSENT for every production run: `putGraphBody` (:125) has ZERO production callers — every call site is a fixture (activation-world-fixtures.ts:310, budget-ledger-fixtures.ts:410/:430, foundation-registry-fixtures.ts:448, graph-query-test-fixtures.ts:458/:468). So there is nothing for the approve leg to recompute the full content hash against.
2. THE SEALED HASH IS A PLACEHOLDER, NOT CODEC OUTPUT. The shipped journey and demo seed both seal graphContentHash = hex64("c0ffee") (bootstrap-test-fixtures.ts:72 journeyAuthority, :345 finalizeChain revision; orchestrator/demo-seed-payloads.ts:37/:320). Rail 1 of eacea969 requires "a recomputed full GraphRevisionContent hash" (encodeGraphContent over all eight design-197/255 fields incl. nodeAuthority, packages/scheduler/src/graph-content.ts:64-76) and forbids equating the structural graphIdentity/snapshotIdentity with it. A placeholder is neither.
3. GRAPH CONTENT BYTES NEVER ENTER THE DAEMON. plan.propose's authority member is exactly {acceptanceContract, planRevision} (planning-authority-persistence.ts:40/:139 → PLANNING_AUTHORITY_MALFORMED otherwise); the planRevision carries only a graphBinding {graphContentHash, graphRevisionRef} (a caller-asserted hash, plan-revision-contract.ts:40-43), never the graph body; finalize refuses caller bodies (planning-authority-finalize-ingress.ts:36 roster; planning-services.ts:120-122 PLANNING_FINALIZE_BODIES_SUPPLIED). eacea969 DoD[2] forbids the approve request from supplying content bytes — so the body must be sealed BEFORE approve runs, and today it is not sealed anywhere.
4. budgetHash/policyHash of the activation binding (GraphActivationBinding, packages/core/src/planning/graph-revision-contract.ts:27-33; PlanningActivationWitness, planning-command-contract.ts:119-128) are NOT derivable from any durable record: sealedHashes carries only {dependencyHash, graphContentHash, planHash, qualityHash} (planning-command-contract.ts:98-103). Candidate durable preimages exist but are unbound to the seal: PolicyDecisionRecord.decisionDigest (policy-contract.ts:143) for policyHash; BudgetAuthorization / requestDigest (budget-ledger-contracts.ts:205/:208) for budgetHash. Whether these become the seal's budget/policy hashes is this row's decision.

DELIVERABLE (measure the exact seam at plan time; this is a producer, not a plan): on the production propose or finalize path, admit or derive the proposed GraphRevisionContent, RECOMPUTE its full graphContentHash via encodeGraphContent (never the structural identity), durably store the body via putGraphBody keyed by that hash, and seal that recomputed hash (plus a durable budget/policy binding source, or an explicit measured decision that the activation binding's budget/policyHash derive from named durable digests) into the run's sealedHashes — so that at approve time readGraphBody answers ok and the recomputed hash equals the sealed hash. NOT in scope: the approve/activation commit itself (eacea969 approve leg), the supersede leg (task-9e52f850), HTTP/MCP wiring (efc2ef63). This may itself decompose (content ingestion vs seal-hash sourcing vs budget/policy binding) — the planner decides via SPIDR.

CONSUMER: task-eacea969's approve leg. This row's landing is what makes DoD[0]'s "commits exactly one ACTIVE revision" recomputable against a real proposal rather than a fixture. Rails carried from eacea969: recompute the FULL hash (never graphIdentity), one durable decision where a decision is committed, no caller-supplied content authority, TDD, per-file line caps, public roots with probed edges.

implementationPlan.description: GREEN 1 — THE INGRESS MODULE: create apps/daemon/src/planning/planning-graph-content-ingress.ts (target ≤150 lines) plus its one-line LF bridge planning-graph-content-ingress.js (`export * from "./planning-graph-content-ingress.ts";`, the convention every sibling follows — a missing bridge reds runtime-entrypoint.test.ts's roster, which the vitest resolver alone never shows). Two own codes, both reachable: PLANNING_GRAPH_CONTENT_MALFORMED (member is not a string, or not canonical standard base64) and PLANNING_GRAPH_CONTENT_HASH_MISMATCH (recompute ≠ the stated hash). Everything else travels VERBATIM from `decodeGraphContent` with its own code and layer. `admitProposedGraphContent({lastCommand, projectId, statedGraphContentHash, store})` returns one of ABSENT | PRESENT | LEG | REFUSED and: reads the member with `ownValue` IMPORTED from planning-authority-finalize-ingress.js (descriptor-safe, no getter invoked — do not restate it); absent → ABSENT; not a string → MALFORMED; decodes base64 with the module-local one-liner the siblings use, then RE-ENCODES the decoded bytes and compares to the input string, refusing MALFORMED on mismatch (`Buffer.from(s,"base64")` never throws on garbage, so without this the malformed arm is vacuous — and non-canonical bytes would change the request bytes the store folds into decision identity, turning a byte-identical retry into IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT instead of REPLAYED); calls `decodeGraphContent(bytes)`, which RE-DERIVES the node-authority set and re-checks the digest — this IS the recompute rail 0 requires, and refusals pass through unrestamped; compares `decoded.value.graphContentHash` to `statedGraphContentHash` and refuses HASH_MISMATCH otherwise; then PRE-READS the body aggregate via `store.readEvents(graphBodyAggregateId(projectId, hash))` and returns PRESENT when a row already exists (event ids are GLOBALLY unique here — emitting `graph-body-${hash}` twice THROWS DurableIdConflictError, the failure that blocked task-16a6a2b1); otherwise returns a LEG `{aggregateId: graphBodyAggregateId(...), events: [{eventId: `graph-body-${hash}`, eventType: GRAPH_BODY_EVENT_TYPE, payload: decoded.value.bytes}], expectedVersion: store.getAggregateVersion(aggregateId)}` — byte-identical to what `putGraphBody` writes, with both the aggregate id and the event type IMPORTED from graph-body-record.js so the durable key derivation exists once.

SHAPE: `admitProposedGraphContent({lastCommand, projectId, statedGraphContentHash, store})` -> `ABSENT | PRESENT | LEG | REFUSED`.
- member read with `ownValue` IMPORTED from planning-authority-finalize-ingress.js — descriptor-safe, no getter invoked, and not restated here so the two seams cannot drift.
- absent -> ABSENT. Not a string, empty, or non-canonical base64 -> PLANNING_GRAPH_CONTENT_MALFORMED @ this layer.
- `decodeGraphContent(bytes)` -> refusals travel out with the CODEC's OWN code and layer, taken from `issues[0]`, unrestamped.
- recompute != stated -> PLANNING_GRAPH_CONTENT_HASH_MISMATCH @ this layer.
- body row already present -> PRESENT; otherwise a LEG whose aggregate id and event type are IMPORTED from graph-body-record.js, so the durable key derivation exists in exactly one place.

TWO CODES ONLY, both reachable from the arms written in step 3. The layer constant is MODULE-PRIVATE and only the closed code roster and the layer TYPE are exported: the security roster scanner keys on column-0 `*_LAYER(S)` exports and would demand a BEFORE/AFTER/RACE trio for one, which this row does not own. That is also why step 8 runs `pnpm test:security` — a row adding an exported code roster is invisible to the other four legs.

THE CANONICAL RE-ENCODE IS THE LOAD-BEARING LINE, and the plan's reason for it is only half of it. `Buffer.from(s,"base64")` NEVER throws — whitespace, the url-safe alphabet and missing padding are all decoded best-effort — so without re-encoding and comparing, the three non-canonical MALFORMED arms would be vacuous. The half worth restating: the request bytes are folded into the DECISION's identity, so admitting two spellings of the same body would turn a byte-identical retry into an IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT instead of a replay. The check is one line and it is drilled by m4.

ONE JUDGEMENT I MADE THAT THE PLAN LEFT OPEN. `canonicalBytes` rejects the EMPTY string and empty decoded bytes as MALFORMED rather than passing them to the codec. Both would otherwise reach `decodeGraphContent`, which refuses them with its own code — so the seam would still fail closed, but the arm asserting "an empty string is MALFORMED at the ingress" would then be asserting the CODEC's verdict under this module's name. Refusing here keeps "which layer answered" true rather than approximately true; the codec-passthrough arm uses truncated REAL codec bytes, which is a body the codec must judge.

THE PRE-READ IS NOT AN OPTIMISATION and the comment says so at the seam: event ids are globally unique in this store, so a second `graph-body-<hash>` THROWS DurableIdConflictError rather than refusing (task-16a6a2b1). Step 3 measured the reachable shape — two RUNS sharing one graph, since the body aggregate is keyed by (project, content) and not by run — and step 7's m6 drill removes the guard to prove the arm catches it.
